rows.grounds: the speaker is also a suitable means
one who knows that scripture also
a fellow disciple of the same teacher

items.question: What serves as the means to knowledge and who can impart it?
premises: The scripture is the means to that knowledge.
The teacher is a suitable speaker and means.
One who knows that scripture, such as a fellow disciple, can give knowledge through dialogue.
items.inference: Knowledge can be transmitted through scripture, the teacher, and dialogue with those who know the scripture.
uncertainties: The exact scope of 'tad' (that) depends on the preceding verses.
items.plain_english: The means to that knowledge is the scripture, and the teacher is a suitable speaker. Even a fellow disciple who knows that scripture can impart knowledge through dialogue.

rows.grounds: not due to birth relation but due to connection with knowledge

items.question: On what basis are the teacher's family members included in the honored group?
premises: The teacher's wife, brother, son, and others form a group.
Their inclusion is not based on birth or family connection.
Their inclusion is based on their connection with knowledge.
items.inference: Membership in the teacher's honored circle depends on a connection with knowledge, not on biological kinship.
items.plain_english: The teacher's wife, brother, son, and others belong to this group not because of birth relations, but because of their connection with knowledge.

rows.grounds: grounded in body and ego formed from the maturation of seed and blood
a lineage that supports the body

items.question: How is the bodily lineage established among blood relatives?
premises: Body and ego are established through the maturation of seed and blood.
This forms a lineage that supports the body.
Such a lineage is fully established among blood relatives.
items.inference: Blood kinship constitutes a bodily lineage rooted in physical generation.
uncertainties: The compound 'vīryāruṇaparīṇāmadehāhantāpratiṣṭhitāḥ' is dense and may admit alternative internal divisions.
items.plain_english: Those established in body and ego through the development of seed and blood form a lineage that supports the body, and this is fully established among blood relatives.

rows.grounds: in the texts of traditional law
the taking of inheritance by lineage
because of the distinction between near and distant relations

items.question: Why is inheritance by lineage considered appropriate in traditional law?
premises: Traditional law texts prescribe inheritance through lineage.
This prescription is fitting because it reflects degrees of closeness.
The distinction between near and distant relations justifies graded inheritance.
items.inference: Inheritance rules in traditional law are grounded in the graded closeness of bodily lineage.
items.plain_english: And so, in the traditional law texts, inheritance by lineage is indeed fitting, since it is determined by the distinction between nearer and more distant relations.

rows.grounds: having abandoned attachment to the body
partaking in awareness and the sense of I
they, through two lineages that support awareness

items.question: What kind of kinship belongs to those who have abandoned attachment to the body?
premises: Some have abandoned attachment to the body.
They partake in shared awareness and a shared sense of I.
They are connected through two lineages that support awareness.
items.inference: For those beyond bodily attachment, kinship is based on shared awareness rather than physical lineage.
uncertainties: The exact nature of the 'two lineages' supporting awareness is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: But those who have abandoned attachment to the body and share in awareness and the sense of I enjoy kinship through two lineages that support awareness.

rows.grounds: in that regard, in this way
whose seeing and acting are opened by the Lord's power
constructed from successive prior material causes

items.question: How is the body understood in relation to prior causes and the Lord's power?
premises: Seeing and acting are opened by the Lord's power.
The body is constructed from successive prior material causes.
This understanding arises in a reflective inquiry into the self.
items.inference: The body is seen as a product of prior material causes, while perception and action depend on the Lord's power.
items.plain_english: In this regard, when one's seeing and acting are opened by the Lord's power, one understands that this body is indeed made from a series of earlier material causes.

rows.grounds: because it is eternal, it is without a cause
again, from its own freedom, this self

items.question: Why does the changeless self appear to be concealed?
premises: The self is free from change and, being eternal, has no cause.
By its own freedom, the self can appear otherwise.
Thus the self remains as if concealed.
items.inference: The self's apparent concealment is due to its own freedom, not to any real change in its nature.
items.plain_english: The self is free from change and, being eternal, has no cause; yet by its own freedom it remains as if concealed.

items.question: What happens when the self becomes manifest again?
premises: The self can become manifest again.
Its manifestation leads to attaining the state of Bhairava.
This manifestation is strongly connected with enjoyment and liberation.
items.inference: The self's re-manifestation culminates in the Bhairava state, which encompasses both enjoyment and liberation.
items.plain_english: And again, when it becomes manifest and attains the state of Bhairava, that manifestation is strongly characterized by both enjoyment and liberation.

rows.grounds: through a stream of such and similar knowledge gradually becoming clear

items.question: What is the suitable means for the manifestation of the self's highest state?
premises: A suitable means is required for the self's manifestation.
That means is the lineage of knowledge.
It operates through a stream of similar knowledge gradually becoming clear.
items.inference: The appropriate means for realization is a gradually clarifying lineage of knowledge.
items.plain_english: The suitable means for this is the lineage of knowledge, operating through a stream of such and similar knowledge that gradually becomes clear.

rows.grounds: through the disappearance of what is of a different kind
and of the knowledge lineage accustomed to beginningless worldly existence

items.question: How is the goal attained quickly through the lineage of knowledge?
premises: The goal is attained when what is of a different kind fades away.
This fading allows the goal to be obtained quickly.
The process transforms a knowledge lineage long accustomed to beginningless worldly existence.
items.inference: By dissolving alien patterns, the knowledge lineage rapidly reaches its goal, even after long worldly conditioning.
items.plain_english: As what is of a different kind fades away, the goal is quickly attained; in this way, even a knowledge lineage long accustomed to beginningless worldly life is transformed.

rows.grounds: the condition of becoming another lineage
of a noble knowledge lineage not accustomed to worldly existence

items.question: What happens to knowledge when the worldly lineage is destroyed?
premises: The destruction of the worldly knowledge lineage occurs.
Transcendent knowledge then arises.
This knowledge takes the form of a different, noble lineage not accustomed to worldly life.
items.inference: When worldly conditioning is destroyed, knowledge shifts into a transcendent lineage.
items.plain_english: When that worldly lineage is destroyed, transcendent knowledge arises and takes on the character of another, noble lineage not accustomed to worldly life.

rows.grounds: that knowledge of the teacher entering the self
through the bestowal of those qualities there

items.question: What is the primary cause of the new transcendent knowledge lineage?
premises: A primary and original cause is required for the new lineage.
That cause is the teacher's knowledge entering the disciple.
It works by clearly bestowing its distinctive qualities.
items.inference: The teacher's transmitted knowledge is the primary cause that establishes the transcendent lineage in the disciple.
items.plain_english: The primary and original cause is the teacher's knowledge entering the self, clearly bestowing its own distinctive qualities.

items.question: How does the knowledge lineage relate to bodily difference and continuity?
premises: The teacher's knowledge functions as a fitting material cause.
Bodies may differ even within a bodily lineage.
The knowledge lineage does not follow the same pattern of difference and non-difference as the body.
items.inference: The continuity of the knowledge lineage is not determined by bodily sameness or difference.
items.plain_english: That knowledge is indeed a fitting material cause; for even when bodies differ, the difference and non-difference that apply to the bodily lineage do not apply in the same way to the lineage of knowledge.

rows.grounds: for being of that same nature
like a corpse-body entered by a yogi's will
in bringing life to another body and so on

items.question: Is animating another body the same as transmitting a knowledge lineage?
premises: A yogi may animate another body by will, like entering a corpse.
Such animation does not establish the same kind of continuity as a knowledge lineage.
The yogi's own body is not abandoned in that process.
items.inference: The transmission of a knowledge lineage is not equivalent to a yogi's temporary animation of another body.
items.plain_english: It is not the same as a yogi animating a corpse-body by will; when a yogi brings life to another body and so on, that does not create the same kind of continuity, since the yogi does not abandon his own body.

rows.grounds: the condition of being the material cause of various knowledges
because the knowledge lineage is primary over the bodily lineage

items.question: Why does the yogi's case not undermine the primacy of the knowledge lineage?
premises: A yogi who does not abandon the body may become the basis for various knowledges.
This does not make bodily continuity primary.
The knowledge lineage remains primary over the bodily lineage.
items.inference: Even in extraordinary yogic cases, the lineage of knowledge retains primacy over bodily continuity.
uncertainties: The rhetorical force of 'na kim' is slightly compressed in translation.
items.plain_english: Even if a yogi, without abandoning the body, becomes the basis for various knowledges, that does not change the fact that the lineage of knowledge is primary over the bodily lineage.

rows.grounds: established in the knowledge of Shiva

items.question: What causal structure supports the teacher lineage established in Shiva knowledge?
premises: There is a mutual lineage of teachers established in Shiva knowledge.
Given this, a threefold causal structure is recognized.
It includes a primary cause and an assisting cause.
items.inference: The teacher lineage grounded in Shiva knowledge is supported by a structured set of causes.
uncertainties: The third member of the 'threefold' set is named explicitly in the next verse.
items.plain_english: Thus, when there is a mutual lineage of teachers established in the knowledge of Shiva, a threefold structure is recognized: a primary cause and an assisting cause.

rows.grounds: sharing one cause and one effect
and a thing of that kind; thus this
is said here to be the cause

items.question: How are the members of the teacher's group classified causally?
premises: The teacher's group is analyzed in terms of cause and effect.
The teacher is identified as the primary cause.
The teacher's wife is identified as the assisting cause.
items.inference: The teacher's circle is organized according to distinct causal roles in the transmission of knowledge.
uncertainties: The phrase 'ekakāraṇakāryaṃ ca vastu' is compact and may also imply a shared single effect.
items.plain_english: Thus the teacher's group is understood in terms of cause and effect: the teacher is the cause, and his wife is the assisting cause.

rows.grounds: there would be eligibility in ritual
of the inner noble power of awareness, the outer counterpart

items.question: Why is the assisting power necessary for ritual eligibility?
premises: Without power, one lacks eligibility in ritual.
The inner noble power of awareness has an outer counterpart.
Ordinarily, ritual action depends on that outer assisting power.
items.inference: Ritual eligibility generally requires the presence of an assisting power corresponding to inner awareness.
items.plain_english: Because one without power would not be eligible for ritual, the outer counterpart of the inner noble power of awareness is ordinarily required.

rows.grounds: would be; and whoever is similar to that

items.question: Can spiritual efficacy exist without an assisting cause, and who counts as a brother in this sense?
premises: A yogi may have capacity even without an assisting cause.
Those born of one cause are brothers.
Anyone similar in that respect may also be counted as such.
items.inference: While an assisting cause is ordinarily needed, a yogi may transcend that need, and spiritual brotherhood extends to those sharing the same causal basis.
items.plain_english: Just as a yogi may have capacity even without an assisting cause, those born of one cause are brothers; and anyone similar to that may also be regarded in the same way.

rows.grounds: also the teacher group through lineage connection

items.question: Which teacher lineage is to be honored above all?
premises: The teacher group may also be spoken of through lineage connection.
Among these, one lineage is primary.
That primary lineage is always to be worshiped and honored.
items.inference: The primary lineage of teachers, defined by true transmission, deserves continual worship and honor.
items.plain_english: Again, the teacher group is also spoken of through lineage connection; but this primary lineage is always to be worshiped and honored.

rows.grounds: for whatever day that is, indeed
a cause of knowledge, means, body, and so forth

items.question: Why are the birth, initiation, and death days of teachers ritually significant?
premises: The days of birth, initiation, and death of teachers and others are marked.
Each of these days is a cause related to knowledge, means, and embodiment.
Such days therefore have ritual significance.
items.inference: The key life-days of teachers are significant because they mark causal moments in the transmission of knowledge and embodiment.
items.plain_english: For teachers and others, the days of birth, initiation, and death are significant, because each of these days is a cause connected with knowledge, the means, the body, and so on.

rows.grounds: of the body that is the cause of such enjoyment, liberation, and so forth

items.question: Why is one's own birthday considered a means of knowledge?
premises: One's own birthday is identified as a means of knowledge.
It is the cause of the body associated with enjoyment and liberation.
That body serves as the basis for spiritual practice and realization.
items.inference: One's birthday is ritually meaningful because it marks the arising of the body that enables knowledge, enjoyment, and liberation.
items.plain_english: Thus one's own birthday is said to be a means of knowledge, because it is the cause of the body through which such enjoyment, liberation, and so on become possible.

rows.grounds: because of the birth of the knowledge lineage

items.question: Why can the day of initiation be regarded as a primary birthday?
premises: Initiation and related rites consecrate one's own self.
Such a rite marks the birth of a knowledge lineage.
Therefore the day of that rite can be called a primary birthday.
items.inference: Initiation functions as a spiritual rebirth because it inaugurates the lineage of knowledge.
items.plain_english: The day on which initiation or a similar consecration of one's self takes place should be regarded as a primary birthday, because it marks the birth of the knowledge lineage.

rows.grounds: because at that time one is non-different from Shiva

items.question: Why is one's own death day treated as an occasional observance for others rather than for oneself?
premises: One's own death day is considered in relation to others.
For others it becomes an occasional observance.
At death, the one who has died is non-different from Shiva.
items.inference: The death day is ritually marked by others because the deceased, being non-different from Shiva, is beyond such observance for himself.
items.plain_english: One's own death day will be an occasional observance for others, because at the time of death one becomes non-different from Shiva.
